# Appeal of Denial — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Emerson Alvarez
**Member ID:** W977514824
**Reference Number:** POC-4E415360FE-32022
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-09
**Governing Policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf)

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which was denied on 2026-08-09 for "incomplete documentation." I am asking for reconsideration of this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in my file contain the specific information the plan's own policy asks for.

## The Plan's Own Standard

Cigna's policy states that:

> "hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

The specific listed conditions I was given in connection with my denial are femoral head/neck fracture and avascular necrosis with collapse. Neither of those describes my situation — my diagnosis is degenerative disease of the hip joint, not a fracture or avascular necrosis. I was not provided with the specific policy language covering degenerative joint disease, so I am not able to quote that section here, and I want to be clear with the reviewer that I am not doing so. I am asking that my documentation be measured against whichever specific listed indication in this policy applies to my diagnosis.

That said, the underlying documentation elements the policy asks to see — functional limitation from pain, and failure of non-surgical management — are the same elements that are already in my chart, and I want to walk through how my records address them.

## How My Records Address the Plan's Documentation Elements

**Function-limiting pain.** The policy describes this as:

> "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

My chart documents 24 months of progressive hip pain, and my most recent exam notes that I ambulate with a cane and am limited to one block — a shorter distance than the two-block example given in the plan's own criteria.

**Loss of function affecting daily activities.** The policy describes this as:

> "◦ loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My chart documents that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted, which is a documented limitation in a basic daily activity.

**Failure of non-surgical management.** The policy describes this as:

> "• Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My chart documents 16 weeks (2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23) of supervised physical therapy (20 visits) focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, 4 months of NSAID use with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-15 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This is more than three months of provider-directed non-surgical management, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

**Imaging.** My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph from 2026-06-02 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes, and my exam shows positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side.

Given this, I do not understand the documentation to be incomplete with respect to duration of symptoms, functional limitation, conservative treatment history, or imaging findings. If the plan needs a specific piece of documentation that is not already in the file — for example, a particular form, note, or test result — I am asking that the denial letter or this appeal response identify exactly what is missing so that my surgeon's office and I can provide it.

## What I Am Asking For

I am requesting that Cigna reconsider this denial and approve prior authorization for total hip replacement (CPT 27130), or, if documentation is still considered incomplete, tell me specifically what is missing so it can be submitted before this appeal deadline.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am submitting it by logging in at my.cigna.com to find the appeal form, and/or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member card, and I will use the mailing address printed on my denial letter if a paper submission is required.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

[Emerson Alvarez]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W977514824

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:

Femoral Head/Neck Fracture • Imaging shows a fracture of the femoral head or femoral neck • Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option Avascular Necrosis (AVN) • Imaging shows avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head • Symptoms include BOTH of the following:

◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration ▪ Criteria exception:
Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate.

◦ loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration ◦ Criteria exception:
The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate.

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Total Hip Replacement Indications CMM.JT.IN.313 v1.0.2026 Total hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:
Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate.

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Revision of Hip Replacement (Partial or Total) Indications CMM.JT.IN.313 v1.0.2026 Revision of hip replacement is considered medically necessary for an individual who has previously undergone a partial or total hip replacement when ANY of the following post-operative conditions are present:

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Salvage Procedures Indications CMM.JT.IN.313 v1.0.2026 Salvage procedures (e.g., Girdlestone acetabuloplasty, hip joint arthrodesis) are considered medically necessary when performed as a surgical alternative in certain individuals for whom primary hip replacement or revision of hip replacement is not a reasonable surgical option due to ANY of the following conditions:
Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate.

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Partial Hip Replacement Non-Indications CMM.JT.NI.313 v1.0.2026 Not Medically Necessary • Partial hip replacement is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication, condition, or when ANY of the following are present:
• Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option.
